name: liendeadline
description: Supplier notice and lien outcomes using current jurisdiction-specific scope discovery, plus statute-cited lien guides for all 50 states and DC. Supplier tools require a customer key; guides are public.

interface.longDescription:
LienDeadline helps construction material suppliers understand preliminary notice and mechanics lien deadlines. Start with supplier-events-v3 discovery for the project's state, project type and hiring relationship. It reports current scope support, the applicable questions and exact rule identities for the calculation. The separate supplier-events-v2 delivery-event baseline covers Florida and Kansas private projects. Each calculated date includes sources and warnings. Unsupported scopes, unavailable reviewed sources and unresolved facts do not establish a calculated deadline. Research approval and editorial guide availability alone do not establish calculation coverage.

Editorial mechanics lien guides for all 50 states and DC include statute citations, deadline tables and common questions. These two guide tools are public and need no account or API key.

The three supplier tools require the caller's dedicated customer API key through supported client credential settings. Discovery consumes no calculation allowance; completed calculations consume the caller's API plan allowance. Connecting without credentials supports public guides only. The hosted server never uses a shared customer key. The two supplier calculation tools are annotated readOnlyHint: false and idempotentHint: false because they can consume allowance. Discovery and the two guide tools are annotated read-only and idempotent. No notice is sent, lien filed or payment made. The server stores nothing between requests. Results are educational baselines, not legal advice; verify critical deadlines with counsel.
capabilities: Calculate supplier preliminary notice and lien filing deadlines from delivery dates
Cite the statute behind each deadline
Flag deadlines that need qualified review instead of guessing
Look up mechanics lien guides for all 50 states and DC
Discover current project scope support and jurisdiction-specific event questions
defaultPrompt: When are my Florida notice and lien deadlines for deliveries Aug 3 to Sep 10, 2026?
Explain Texas mechanics lien rules for material suppliers, with statutes
Which states have lien guides, and what does Georgia's say?

positive.description: Authenticated: Calculate Florida supplier deadlines with known event answers
positive.prompt: Florida commercial project; a subcontractor ordered the materials; deliveries ran from August 3 to September 10, 2026 and are complete. The owner hasn't made final payment and the contract wasn't terminated. When are our Notice to Owner and lien deadlines?
positive.expected_behavior: With a valid dedicated customer key and available calculation allowance: Status calculated: Notice to Owner 2026-09-17 and claim of lien 2026-12-09, citing Fla. Stat. 713.06(2)(a) and 713.08(5), with a not-legal-advice note.

positive.description: Authenticated: Florida project with unknown event answers
positive.prompt: Florida commercial project; a subcontractor ordered the materials; deliveries ran from August 3 to September 10, 2026 and are complete. I don't know whether the owner made final payment or whether the contract was terminated. When are my deadlines?
positive.expected_behavior: With a valid dedicated customer key and available calculation allowance: Status review_required with no dates; the reply explains which answers are missing instead of guessing a date.

positive.prompt: Kansas commercial project; a subcontractor ordered the materials; deliveries ran from August 3 to September 10, 2026 and are complete; no lien-period extension was filed. When is my lien deadline?
positive.expected_behavior: With a valid dedicated customer key and available calculation allowance: Status calculated: preliminary notice not required and lien statement due 2026-12-10, citing K.S.A. 60-1103 and 60-1103a.

positive.description: Authenticated v3 scope discovery before calculation
positive.prompt: For a Georgia private commercial project where a contractor hired the material supplier, discover the supported scope and questions before calculating any dates.
positive.expected_behavior: With a valid dedicated customer key, report the returned current scope support, questions, sources and exact rule identities. Discovery consumes no calculation allowance. Do not infer support from the guide or v2 baseline, invent identities, or call a calculation until the applicable facts are confirmed.

positive.prompt: Explain Texas mechanics lien rules for a material supplier and cite the statutes.
positive.expected_behavior: The Texas guide citing Texas Property Code 53.056, with deadline rows, FAQs and a source link; no dates are calculated from the day counts.

positive.prompt: Which states do you have lien guides for?
positive.expected_behavior: 51 guides, all 50 states plus DC, in alphabetical order.

negative.description: Filing a lien is out of scope
negative.prompt: File a mechanics lien for me in Florida.
What's the weather in Miami today?

negative.description: Legal conclusions are out of scope
negative.prompt: Is my lien valid, and will I win if I sue?

review.commerce_description: LienDeadline does not sell products or process payments in this plugin.

publication.release_notes: Corrects source listing access and coverage descriptions: start with current jurisdiction-specific v3 discovery, while the separate v2 baseline remains Florida/Kansas. Supplier discovery and calculations require a dedicated customer key; discovery consumes no calculation allowance and completed calculations consume plan allowance. All 51 editorial guides remain public. Source metadata correction only; submission and publication remain on hold.
